propositions.text: If returned to Turkey, he will be persecuted for political opinion and religion
Refugee Protection Division refused claim due to lack of credibility and Article 1E exclusion
He appeals to the Refugee Appeal Division

paragraphs.summary: The applicant claims persecution in Turkey; the earlier decision-maker refused protection due to credibility and Article 1E; the applicant appeals.

propositions.text: Confirms RPD decision that appellant is not a refugee or person in need of protection; appeal dismissed

paragraphs.summary: The court confirms the earlier decision and dismisses the appeal.

propositions.text: Claims membership in Kurdish party HDP and Alevi organizations
Claims detention, interrogation and torture by Turkish authorities due to political activities
Applied for Canadian visa via agent/smuggler using documents claiming residence and work in Germany
Arrived in Canada and made inland refugee claim on March 27, 2017

paragraphs.summary: The applicant claims political and religious membership, alleges torture, used documents claiming German residence to get visa, and made refugee claim in Canada.

propositions.text: Requests admission of two new documents: German Consulate letter and affidavit from friend Mr. XXXX

paragraphs.summary: The applicant requests admission of two new documents at appeal.

propositions.text: Subsection 110(4) IRPA limits new evidence admission to evidence arising after RPD rejection, not reasonably available before, or not reasonably expected to be presented
RAD rule 3(3)(g)(iii) requires detailed submissions on how new evidence meets subsection 110(4) and relates to appellant
If admissible, must consider Singh factors: newness, credibility, relevance
Threshold for new evidence admission before RAD is high

paragraphs.summary: The court states the legal rules for admitting new evidence under IRPA and RAD rules, including Singh factors and high threshold.

propositions.text: Appellant offers no explanation why German Consulate letter was not obtained before RPD rejection
No argument why letter was not reasonably available or expected to be presented before RPD rejection

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the appellant did not explain why the German Consulate letter was not obtained or presented before the RPD rejection.

propositions.text: Fairness requires examining background: hearing adjourned to allow Ministry to contact German authorities with appellant's permission
Ministry declined to intervene after receiving permission
Reasonable for appellant not to contact German authorities given Ministry's initial interest
Appellant could not reasonably have been expected to present German Consulate letter at RPD rejection

paragraphs.summary: The court finds fairness requires considering Ministry's initial interest; thus appellant could not reasonably present the German Consulate letter earlier.

propositions.text: German Consulate letter is credible, new, and highly relevant to RPD's finding of German residency
Letter is admissible as new evidence

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the German Consulate letter credible, new, relevant, and admits it as evidence.

propositions.text: Appellant offers no argument how affidavit from Mr. XXXX meets subsection 110(4)
Affidavit contains no information unavailable before RPD rejection
Affidavit is inadmissible

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the affidavit inadmissible as appellant offers no argument and it contains no new information.

propositions.text: Requests RAD hearing on new evidence, citing affidavit and RPD's failure to address credibility

paragraphs.summary: The applicant requests a hearing before RAD on new evidence and credibility issues.

propositions.text: Subsection 110(3) IRPA requires RAD to proceed without hearing unless subsection 110(6) conditions met
Subsection 110(6) allows hearing if new evidence raises serious credibility issue, is central, and justifies claim outcome

paragraphs.summary: The court states the legal standard for holding a hearing on new evidence under IRPA subsections 110(3) and 110(6).

propositions.text: Affidavit is inadmissible, so subsection 110(6) conditions need not be considered for it
German Consulate letter does not justify allowing or rejecting claim despite impact on Article 1E exclusion
Credibility issue remains despite admitted letter

paragraphs.summary: The court finds affidavit inadmissible and German Consulate letter insufficient to justify claim outcome; credibility remains an issue.

propositions.text: Whether appellant is excluded under Article 1E due to German residency
Credibility of appellant

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies the key issues as Article 1E exclusion and appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: Standard of review is correctness except where RPD has advantage assessing oral testimony, then reasonableness applies

paragraphs.summary: The court states the standard of review as correctness or reasonableness depending on RPD's advantage.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant had permanent residence in Germany and lacked credibility due to falsified passport
Appellant argues he was not German resident and RPD erred on credibility finding

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found German residency and lack of credibility; the appellant disputes both findings.

propositions.text: RPD found visa application documents authentic and appellant had permanent German residency

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the visa documents authentic and appellant a German resident.

propositions.text: Argues visa application documents except passport were forgeries
Argues RPD erred in assuming visa officials verified document genuineness
Documents may have fooled visa officers but not genuine

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the visa documents were forged and RPD erred in assuming their genuineness.

propositions.text: Admitted German Consulate letter shows residency card was invalid
Letter appears authentic
RPD's finding of permanent German residency is undermined and must be reviewed

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the German Consulate letter authentic and undermining RPD's residency finding, requiring review.

propositions.text: Other visa documents not found invalid
Residency card invalid means appellant not a German resident on balance of probabilities
RPD erred in finding Article 1E exclusion due to German residency

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant not a German resident and that RPD erred in applying Article 1E exclusion.

propositions.text: RPD found two versions of appellant's passport, one with extensive travel, one with altered pages

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found two versions of the appellant's passport with discrepancies.

propositions.text: RPD suggested two versions of passport exist because real passport was modified to hide German connections
Appellant denied knowledge of fraud and attributed it to agent/smuggler
RPD rejected Appellant's explanation and noted Canadian officials would have noticed tampering before visa issuance

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the passport was modified to hide German connections; the Appellant denied knowledge and blamed smugglers; the RPD rejected this explanation.

propositions.text: Appellant claims he provided valid passport to smuggler but never travelled outside Turkey
How to reconcile passport with travel stamps and Appellant's claim of no travel outside Turkey
Appellant argues RPD erred in assuming Canadian official verified genuineness of documents

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant claims he gave a valid passport and never travelled outside Turkey; he argues RPD erred in assuming Canadian officials verified document genuineness.

propositions.text: Examined two passport versions and confirmed they differ in passport numbers on various pages
Canadian visa linked to passport number XXXX; other pages show inconsistent numbers

paragraphs.summary: The court confirmed the two passport versions differ in passport numbers on pages; Canadian visa linked to one number, others inconsistent.

propositions.text: On balance of probabilities, passport submitted to Canadian visa officials was authentic
If clumsily modified version had been submitted, visa officials would have noticed

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the passport submitted to Canadian visa officials was authentic and tampered version would have been noticed.

propositions.text: Version submitted with refugee claim had substituted pages removing travel evidence
On balance of probabilities, there was an attempt to fraudulently modify the passport to hide travel stamps

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the refugee claim passport had substituted pages to hide travel stamps, indicating fraudulent modification.

propositions.text: Appellant says agent/smuggler modified passport and replaced pages after visa process
Whether agent/smuggler could have modified passport after visa officials returned it but before returning to Appellant
Such scenario is implausible and illogical as it would show altered passport at Canadian border

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant claims smugglers modified passport after visa process; court finds this implausible and illogical due to border checks.

propositions.text: Implausible that CBSA officials would not have noticed clumsily doctored passport at entry
On balance of probabilities, Appellant travelled to Canada on unaltered passport

paragraphs.summary: The court finds it implausible CBSA missed doctored passport and concludes Appellant travelled on unaltered passport.

propositions.text: On balance of probabilities, Appellant tampered with passport after arrival in Canada before refugee claim
Appellant may have removed travel evidence to strengthen refugee claim
This fraud seriously undermines Appellant's credibility

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes Appellant tampered with passport after arrival to hide travel, seriously undermining his credibility.

propositions.text: Travel stamps showing extensive travel including Germany are valid
Appellant's testimony denying travel outside Turkey is fabricated
Fabrication seriously undermines Appellant's credibility

paragraphs.summary: The court finds travel stamps valid, Appellant's denial fabricated, and this seriously undermines his credibility.

propositions.text: Before final credibility finding, court reviews supporting documents submitted to RPD
Documents include Turkish identity card, membership receipts, letter, and photographs

paragraphs.summary: The court reviews supporting documents including identity card, membership receipts, letter, and photos before final credibility finding.

propositions.text: Receipts for HDP membership fees appear valid and support Appellant's claim of membership

paragraphs.summary: The court finds HDP membership fee receipts valid and supportive of Appellant's membership claim.

propositions.text: Pir Sultan Abdal Cultural Association membership fees and card appear valid and support Appellant's Alevi Muslim claim

paragraphs.summary: The court finds membership fees and card from cultural association valid and supportive of Appellant's Alevi Muslim claim.

propositions.text: Letter from Canadian Alevi Culture Centre states Appellant is Alevi member since March 2017
Letter's basis for membership finding is unclear but has some probative value

paragraphs.summary: The court notes letter stating Appellant's Alevi membership with unclear basis but assigns some probative value.

propositions.text: Six photographs submitted do not clearly show Appellant; first three show protests with many people
Photos have no probative value; other three photos of limited probative value as Canadian events don't prove Turkish participation

paragraphs.summary: The court finds photos do not clearly show Appellant and have limited or no probative value regarding his claims.

propositions.text: Weighing fraudulent behavior against documents, Appellant is overall lacking credibility
Appellant's claims of persecution by Turkish state on HDP basis are, on balance, false

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Appellant lacks credibility and his persecution claims on HDP basis are false on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Despite credibility findings, court must consider if Alevi Muslims face serious persecution or harm in Turkey

paragraphs.summary: The court must consider if Alevi Muslims face serious persecution or harm in Turkey despite Appellant's credibility issues.

propositions.text: Reviewed Appellant's documents and National Documentation Package; only two articles relate to Alevi situation
Articles are of limited value; one from 1993, other briefly mentions 2016 attack

paragraphs.summary: The court reviewed documents and found only two limited-value articles relating to Alevi situation in Turkey.

propositions.text: Alevi Muslims face inequalities including lack of official worship recognition, education issues, and ID card religion restrictions
Some reports of ill-treatment mainly during demonstrations; isolated societal discrimination and violence reported
Most Alevis coexist with other communities with few daily problems

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Alevi Muslims face inequalities and some ill-treatment but mostly coexist peacefully with others.

propositions.text: UK Home Office summary: Alevi treatment does not generally amount to persecution or serious harm
Court agrees Alevi Muslims generally do not face serious possibility of persecution in Turkey

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with UK Home Office that Alevi treatment in Turkey generally does not amount to persecution or serious harm.

propositions.text: Appellant will not face serious possibility of persecution on return to Turkey
On balance, Appellant will not face harm described in subsection 97(1) of IRPA

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes Appellant will not face serious persecution or harm under IRPA on return to Turkey.

propositions.text: The Appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal.
